name: wraps greedily without subjective reflow
test:
assert format_articles(['one two three'], 7) == ['one two', 'three']
assert format_articles(['  one\t two\nthree  '], 7) == ['one two', 'three']

name: moves the preceding word with its punctuation onto the next line
input: punctuation group cannot fit on the current line
test:
assert format_articles(['one two , next'], 7) == ['one', 'two ,', 'next']
assert format_articles(['Hi Hello ,world next'], 12) == ['Hi', 'Hello ,world', 'next']

name: accepts exact-width groups and consecutive punctuation tokens
input: one indivisible group with several punctuation-leading tokens
test:
assert format_articles(['Hello ,world'], 12) == ['Hello ,world']
assert format_articles(['a b , ! c'], 5) == ['a', 'b , !', 'c']

name: places structural separators between articles including empty ones
input: empty articles and separator wider than text width
test:
assert format_articles(['First', '', 'Third'], 20) == ['First', '----', '----', 'Third']
assert format_articles(['a', '', 'b'], 1) == ['a', '----', '----', 'b']
assert format_articles([], 20) == []
assert format_articles(['', ''], 2) == ['----']

name: rejects words and punctuation groups that cannot fit
input: impossible long word or indivisible group

name: rejects leading punctuation and invalid width
input: punctuation has no predecessor or width is nonpositive
